prompt:
Reddit post, r/houseplants.
Title: Is this new vine stuck or am I just too impatient?

I took some cuttings from this scindapsus a while ago (they are doing great). Now the mother plant is forming a new vine from the last node before I cut it, but the tip seems to be stuck. Do I need to do something or just wait?

What is wrong with my plant?
answer:
Nothing is wrong. The growing tip is just a new leaf still rolled up as it unfurls, which is how Scindapsus pictus (silver satin pothos) grows. The leaf and stem are firm, bright green, and not mushy or discolored, and the spotted leaves elsewhere on the plant look healthy.

Just wait. New leaves on this plant can take one to three weeks to fully open, and the tip may look stuck for part of that time.

Do not unwrap or pull on the leaf, since that can tear it. Keep the plant where it is, with bright indirect light, and water only when the top inch of soil is dry.

If the tip turns brown, soft, or black, or the stem above the leaf collapses, come back and post a photo. Otherwise, your cuttings and mother plant appear to be doing well.
